apps: it lists what is installed, and nothing on the screen changes.
background: the app is off the screen for the seconds it is away, and back in front when the command returns.
clear-data: it deletes an app's data, which shows only the next time the app starts.
crashes: it reads the device's crash reports, and nothing on the screen changes.
current: it names the app in front, and nothing on the screen changes.
daemon: the daemon runs on this machine, not the device.
daemon-start: the daemon runs on this machine, not the device.
daemon-status: the daemon runs on this machine, not the device.
daemon-stop: the daemon runs on this machine, not the device.
daemon-up: the daemon runs on this machine, not the device.
devices: it lists the devices this machine can see.
dialogs: a rule does nothing when it is declared; it answers a dialog that gets in the way of a later action, and that action's answer says so.
doctor: it checks this machine, and needs no device.
grant: it changes what an app may do, not what is on the screen; the next dialog that does not appear is the evidence.
install: it installs an app, which shows nowhere until the app is launched.
lock: a locked emulator's screen is off, so its screenshot is black.
logs: it reads a log, and nothing on the screen changes.
record: what it keeps is a video of the screen.
reset-permissions: it changes what an app may do, not what is on the screen.
revoke: it changes what an app may do, not what is on the screen.
session: a session is the connection to the device, and the screen shows nothing of it.
shake: an emulator shows nothing for a shake; whether the app reacts is up to the app.
source: it reads the hierarchy, and nothing on the screen changes.
state: it reads whether an app is running, and nothing on the screen changes.
time: it reads the device's clock, and nothing on the screen changes.
uninstall: it removes an app, which shows nowhere on the screen in front.
